blocks.content: 1.1 Ancient History of Goa

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Early Goan history saw rule under major dynasties including the Mauryas, Satavahanas, Bhojas, and prominently the Kadamba Dynasty (960–1312 CE).
Control over Goa shifted between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Bahamani Sultanate during the medieval period prior to European arrival.
Afonso de Albuquerque led the Portuguese conquest of Goa in 1510, initiating over four centuries of colonial occupation.
The oppressive Goa Inquisition enforced strict religious suppression from 1560 to 1812.
India successfully liberated Goa through the military action known as Operation Vijay on December 18–19, 1961.

blocks.content: Goa has one of the oldest recorded histories in India. Archaeological evidence suggests human habitation in Goa dating back to the Palaeolithic and Neolithic ages. The region finds mention in the Mahabharata as 'Goparashtra' (land of cowherds) and in early Sanskrit texts as 'Gomant' or 'Gomantak'.
1.1.1 Pre-Historic Period

Rock carvings (petroglyphs) at Usgalimal on the banks of River Kushavati are believed to be over 20,000 years old. These include images of animals, geometric patterns, and human figures. The site was discovered in 1993 and is one of the most significant pre-historic sites in South Asia.

items: Petroglyphs discovered at Usgalimal (Sanguem Taluka) dating to Late Pleistocene
The Konkan Coast including Goa was inhabited since Mesolithic times
Ancient settlements found along River Zuari and River Mandovi
Goa mentioned as 'Gomanta' in Skanda Purana

blocks.content: 1.1.2 Early Medieval Period — Maurya, Satavahana, and Bhojas

Goa was part of the Mauryan Empire during the reign of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (322-298 BCE) and his grandson Ashoka. After the Mauryas, the Satavahanas (230 BCE – 220 CE) controlled the region. The Bhojas of South Konkan were an early ruling dynasty.

cells: Goa was part of the vast Mauryan territory; Buddhism spread
Controlled the Konkan coast; important trade links with Rome
Local dynasty; early rulers of South Konkan including Goa
Extended control to Goa; Goa was called 'Chandrapur'
Goa was a prosperous trading port under Rashtrakutas
Feudatory of Rashtrakutas; ruled parts of Goa
First native dynasty to rule Goa independently; capital at Chandor then Goa-Velha

blocks.content: 1.1.3 The Kadamba Dynasty (960–1312 CE)

The Kadamba dynasty was the first independent native ruling dynasty of Goa. Their kingdom flourished between the 10th and 14th centuries CE. They are considered the original rulers of Goa and made significant contributions to trade, culture, and administration.

items: Founded by Shasthadeva around 960 CE
Capital initially at Chandrapur (modern Chandor) and later at Govepuri (Goa-Velha)
Goa was known as 'Gomanchala' during their reign
Excellent traders — had active ports and conducted trade with Arab merchants
Built many temples and inscriptions in Nagari and Kannada scripts
Jayakeshi I (1050–1080 CE) was the most notable ruler — he gave Goa its golden age
The Kadamba dynasty ended when Goa was captured by Muhammad bin Tughluq in 1312 CE

blocks.content: 1.2 Medieval History of Goa
1.2.1 Vijayanagara Empire and Bahamani Sultanate
Liberation of Goa — Operation Vijay (December 18–19, 1961)

After the decline of the Kadambas, Goa passed through the hands of multiple powers. The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1565 CE) and the Bahamani Sultanate (1347–1527 CE) were the two dominant powers competing for control over Goa.

items: Vijayanagara rulers used Goa as their primary port for importing horses from Arabia
Horses were imported for the Vijayanagara cavalry through Goa's ports
The Bahmani Sultanate captured Goa in 1470 under Mahmud Gawan
After the split of the Bahmani Sultanate, the Adil Shahis of Bijapur controlled Goa from 1490
Yusuf Adil Shah established his summer capital at Goa

blocks.content: 1.2.2 Portuguese Arrival and Conquest (1510)

The arrival of the Portuguese marks the most significant turning point in Goa's history. Alfonso de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate on November 25, 1510 — a date still celebrated as 'Goa Liberation Day' in Goa (though this is distinct from the 1961 liberation from Portugal). The capture is sometimes referred to as the first conquest.

cells: Opens sea route from Europe to India
One of the most notorious in history

blocks.content: 1.2.3 Portuguese Colonial Rule

The Portuguese ruled Goa for 451 years — the longest colonial rule of any territory in the Indian subcontinent. Their rule fundamentally changed the social, religious, cultural, and architectural landscape of Goa.
Key features of Portuguese colonial administration:

rows: Promoted regional maritime trade and indigenous culture
Colonial administrative system, spice trade control, and Goa Inquisition
Ended by Indian Armed Forces via Operation Vijay

items: Goa became the capital of the 'Estado da India' (Portuguese State of India)
The Viceroy was the head of Portuguese India, based at Goa
Goa at its height was known as 'Goa Dourada' (Golden Goa)
Pope Paul III established the Goa Diocese in 1534
St. Francis Xavier arrived in Goa in 1542 — his body is preserved at Bom Jesus Basilica
The Goa Inquisition (1560–1812) was used to persecute non-Christians
During the 16th–17th centuries, Goa was the wealthiest and most cosmopolitan city in Asia

blocks.content: 1.2.4 The Goa Inquisition (1560–1812)

The Goa Inquisition was one of the most brutal religious inquisitions in history. Established in 1560 by the Portuguese at the request of Francis Xavier, it aimed to enforce Christianity and punish heresy, apostasy, and other religious offences.

items: Established in 1560 under Francisco Barreto as the first Governor-General
Operated from the 'Palacio da Inquisicao' in Old Goa
Thousands of Hindus and converted Christians were tried, tortured, and executed
Hindu temples were demolished; over 300 temples destroyed in Old Goa area alone
Suppression of Hindu festivals, rituals, and customs
Officially abolished in 1812 under pressure from the British

blocks.content: 1.3 Freedom Movement and Liberation of Goa
1.3.1 Early Resistance
Resistance to Portuguese rule began almost from the beginning. The Ranes of Satari conducted 16 revolts between 1650 and 1912. Other notable uprisings include:

items: Pinto Revolt (1787) — Led by Father Jose Custodio Faria and other Goan intellectuals
The revolt inspired by the French Revolution; suppressed brutally
Abbé Faria later became famous as a pioneer of hypnotism in France
The Rane Revolts (1852–1912) — The most sustained resistance in North Goa
Dipubai Rane and Dada Rane were prominent leaders

blocks.content: 1.3.2 The 20th Century Freedom Movement

items: Operation Vijay took place on December 18–19, 1961, ending 451 years of Portuguese rule in Goa.
The Goa Inquisition lasted from 1560 to 1812 and is a frequently asked historical timeline item in competitive exams.
The Kadamba Dynasty (960–1312 CE) represents a major regional ruling power in ancient/medieval Goan history.

blocks.content: The Goa freedom movement gained momentum in the 20th century, inspired by India's independence struggle. Several organizations worked for Goa's liberation:

items: Goa Congress Committee formed in 1928
Tristao de Braganza Cunha — called the 'Father of Goan Nationalism'
He was imprisoned multiple times for anti-colonial activities
Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia launched a Satyagraha in Goa in 1946
National Congress (Goa) formed in 1947 after India's independence
First batch of satyagrahis entered Goa in 1955; many were imprisoned or killed

blocks.content: 1.3.3 Liberation of Goa — Operation Vijay (December 18–19, 1961)

Despite India's independence in 1947, Goa remained under Portuguese control. After years of diplomatic pressure and internal struggle, the Indian Government launched Operation Vijay on December 18, 1961.
December 19 is celebrated as 'Goa Liberation Day' — a state public holiday every year.

items: Goa was first administered as a Union Territory along with Daman and Diu
The Goa, Daman and Diu Administration Act, 1962 governed the territory
The Opinion Poll of 1967 decided that Goa should remain a Union Territory (and not merge with Maharashtra)
Goa was granted statehood on May 30, 1987 under the 56th Constitutional Amendment
Daman and Diu became a separate Union Territory at the time of Goa's statehood
